## Problem

## Requirements

- **Input:** a nonnegative integer array `height[]`; the value `height[i]` gives the height of the vertical segment positioned at x-coordinate `i`.
- **Output:** return the greatest water-container area, computed as `max over (i, j) of (j - i) * min(height[i], height[j])`.
- Report only that maximum area; do not return the pair of positions.

## Preparation

- Work through LeetCode 11, "Container With Most Water," and be ready to explain in one paragraph why the shorter-side pointer must be advanced.
- Practice the related LeetCode 42, "Trapping Rain Water," as a possible follow-up; it relies on similar two-pointer thinking but targets a different result.
- Rehearse describing your reasoning aloud while implementing the code, since the OCI interviewer treated that discussion as a light behavioral signal.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

The area is limited by the shorter line, so moving the taller line inward can never increase the area—focus on the shorter one.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use two pointers starting at the ends, moving the pointer with the smaller height inward to potentially find a larger area.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Complexity is O(n) time and O(1) space, the key insight is that you only need to consider each pair once.

</details>
